families.label: Hypercubes
families.note: The measure polytopes. Every edge runs along an axis, which is exactly what a square module grid samples cleanly, and is why this family is the one the prototype is built around.

rejected.why: An angle that is neither 0 nor 45, so every edge becomes a dotted stagger.

families.label: Cross-polytopes
families.note: The duals of the hypercubes: vertices on the axes, every non-opposite pair joined. Several vertices project to the same point, so they read as a figure inside a diamond rather than as nested cells.

families.label: Duoprisms
families.note: An m-gon times a k-gon. The angles available are the polygons' own, so octagons work (every edge on an axis or a 45) and triangles do not.

rejected.why: The triangular ring's edges never land on 0, 45 or 90; they staircase the way the octagonal ones do not.

families.label: Simplexes
families.note: The minimum solid in each dimension. No two edges are parallel and none aligns to an axis, which is the one thing this grid cannot draw.

rejected.why: No axis to align to, so its edges staircase at every angle.

families.label: The 24-cell
families.note: Self-dual, 96 edges, and no analogue in any other dimension — it is its own family. The densest subject here that still reads.

rejected.why: Fills solid. 96 edges with no gaps left for a reader.
